title: Best Prom Ever
cn: 第 20 集 · 最棒的毕业舞会
novel:
Barney needed to hear a band play, and the band was booked for a high-school [[prom|prom]]. So the adults decided to [[gatecrash|gatecrash]] it.

They wore a poor [[disguise|disguise]]: old jackets, and a plastic [[corsage|corsage]] for Lily, who claimed to be a [[chaperone|chaperone]].

Inside, the school hall was gloriously [[tacky|tacky]]. Silver [[glitter|glitter]] covered the floor. A wall of blue [[balloons|balloon]] hid the basketball nets. Every dress had a thousand [[sequins|sequin]], and a paper [[crown|crown]] waited on a table for the king of the night.

Every [[teenager|teenager]] in the room looked [[insecure|insecure]]. They stood in tight little [[cliques|clique]], watching the door, [[yearning|yearn]] for somebody to notice them.

Watching a [[slow dance|slow dance]], Ted felt something [[bittersweet|bittersweet]]. He had spent his own teenage years waiting to become a [[grown-up|grown-up]], and now he stood here, older, still waiting for his life to start.

The children were [[innocent|innocent]] and [[fond|fond]] of everything. They would [[cherish|cherish]] this [[memorable|memorable]] night for twenty years.

At eleven the [[curfew|curfew]] emptied the hall. The adults walked out into the street, quiet, smiling, and slightly embarrassed by how much they had enjoyed it.

prom.en: a big formal dance for students at the end of high school

gatecrash.en: to go to a party without being invited

disguise.en: clothes you wear so people do not know who you are

corsage.en: a small bunch of flowers worn on a dress or wrist

chaperone.en: an adult who watches young people at an event

glitter.en: tiny shiny bits used to decorate things

balloon.en: a coloured rubber bag filled with air

sequin.en: a small shiny disc sewn onto clothes

crown.en: the round thing a king or queen wears on the head

teenager.en: a young person between 13 and 19 years old

insecure.cn: 缺乏自信的；心里没底的
insecure.en: not confident; worried that you are not good enough

clique.en: a small group of friends who keep others out

yearn.en: to want something very much, in a sad way

slow dance.en: a dance to slow music, holding your partner

bittersweet.en: happy and sad at the same time

innocent.en: having no experience of bad things

fond.cn: 喜爱的（常用 be fond of）
fond.en: liking someone or something very much

cherish.en: to love something and keep it carefully

memorable.en: so good or special that you will remember it

curfew.en: a time by which you must be home or off the streets
